mcat_description.short: Prefabricated school buildings are factory-manufactured, modular educational structures built using steel frames (LGSF or mild steel) with insulated sandwich panel walls and roofs, supplied as complete turnkey units ready for on-site assembly.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated school buildings are engineered modular structures where components — steel frames, insulated wall and roof panels, doors, windows, and MEP systems — are manufactured off-site in a factory and assembled on-site, significantly reducing construction time versus conventional RCC methods. The dominant structural technology in the Indian market is Light Gauge Steel Framing (LGSF) combined with PUF or EPS insulated sandwich panels, though mild steel frame variants with cement board or PPGL cladding are also widely supplied. These buildings are designed to comply with Indian building codes including IS 1893 for seismic resistance and relevant fire safety standards, and are available in single-storey and multi-storey configurations with customisable layouts for classrooms, labs, staff rooms, and sanitation blocks. Buyers typically procure on a turnkey basis — covering design, fabrication, transport, and installation — and quote requirements in square feet of built-up area.

market_context: Prefabricated school buildings in India are a growing segment driven by government infrastructure programmes (SSA, NEP 2020), NGO-led rural education initiatives, and private school expansion demand. The dominant structural technology is Light Gauge Steel Framing (LGSF) combined with PUF or EPS insulated sandwich panels, as adopted by leading manufacturers including EPACK Prefab and Tata Steel Nest-In (HabiNest); mild steel frame variants with sandwich panel or cement board cladding are also widely available from smaller manufacturers. Buildings are engineered to comply with IS 1893 (seismic design) and relevant Indian building codes for structural integrity and fire safety. The supply model is predominantly turnkey — covering design, factory fabrication, transport, and on-site assembly — with buyers quoting requirements in square feet of built-up area. Key manufacturing hubs include Ghaziabad (UP), Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Indore, and Ahmedabad. Buyers compare structures on structural frame type, wall panel insulation type, floor area, storey count, lifespan, seismic compliance, and whether MEP (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) is included in the scope.

research_strategy_consumed.reason: Prefabricated school buildings are engineered structures subject to BIS standards (IS:875, IS:1893 for seismic design) and state building codes. Buyers evaluate structural compliance, material specs, and assembly methodology — not brand names. Agent 3 should prioritise BIS/NFHS standards, state-level building regulations, and technical specification catalogues from manufacturers.
